diagnosis.testedChange: Optional model-written bound source-site fragments versus ordinary whole-source repair, both replaying the identical observed live first candidate through existing R3 under unchanged V3 quality admission.
conclusions: Four unique initial trials were live and privately graded. Three passed functional checks; none passed full quality admission. Two objectives and two repeats are not four independent domains.

All eight declared arm stages executed. Seven dispatched live repairs; the last treatment refused locally at the unchanged prompt bound. That stage retained an earlier artifact but produced no new live candidate.

Neither arm produced a fully accepted repair. Three treatment calls offered 32 bound sites each; the model selected zero and emitted ordinary whole source. There is no causal evidence that source-site cognition improved outcomes.
Three actual treatments used approximately twice the repair tokens of their paired controls, and the fourth used none. No pair matched realized compute within the frozen tolerance.

One treatment quality-repair response broke public behavior and reduced private correctness from 7/12 to 2/12. Functional and structural quality failures coexist; a single primary failure label is not an exhaustive causal diagnosis.

All eleven actual provider calls delivered with reported usage, zero retries, zero provider failures and no observed repair syntax/schema/truncation errors. The fourth treatment's local refusal is not a provider failure or a complete live pair.
Raw generated source was deliberately not retained. Digests, structural measurements and grades do not establish the exact faulty statement or a proof that compact prompting improves model reasoning.
diagnosis.nextGeneralInvestigation: Fresh transfer of compact source-bound presentation under unchanged checks and defensible realized-compute accounting; then a bounded data-only procedure-synthesis hypothesis through the existing workbench, not arbitrary generated-tool execution. Do not rerun exposed frozen tasks for cognitive promotion.
